recommendation: Keep the audit commit. No core source follow-up is needed unless Pharmacy reopens the broader MedicationStatement status/adherence design; any future change should start from the later FHIR-39271/FHIR-32060 model rather than the DSTU1 status-code shape alone.
issue_request: FHIR-7583 was Published/Persuasive with Modification and asked for MedicationStatement.status to distinguish medication-use states such as active versus discontinued, because the original status appeared to reflect the record rather than the medication.
initial_application: FHIR-7583 comments say the issue was fixed as part of FHIR-6310 in svn 6552. Git commit d3c2a3a055 applied that shared status-spreadsheet change, and 31e9678a6e immediately refined the status set to active, completed, entered-in-error, and intended with medication-use definitions.
additional_context: Later Published Pharmacy issues superseded the old status model: FHIR-19468/FHIR-19470 moved taking/not-taking semantics to adherence, FHIR-32060 redesigned status to recorded/entered-in-error/draft, FHIR-38682 renamed MedicationUsage back to MedicationStatement while preserving the model, and FHIR-39271 reaffirmed that status is statement-record status while adherence carries taking/not-taking information.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit. The current build-scope MedicationStatement source already says status concerns recording the medication statement and points to MedicationStatement.adherence, whose example codes include taking, not-taking, stopped, and on-hold. Reintroducing active/discontinued status codes would conflict with later final decisions.

related_jiras.note: FHIR-7583 was applied under this tracker; svn 6552/commit d3c2a3a055 made the shared MedicationStatement status update.

Established recorded, entered-in-error, and draft as the redesigned statement-record status codes.
Reaffirmed that MedicationStatement.status reflects recording status and MedicationStatement.adherence reflects whether medication is being taken.
Renamed MedicationUsage back to MedicationStatement while preserving the later status/adherence model.
